# rmai

Use [mai](https://github.com/mai-lib/mai), the compiled statistical
computing language from Brendan McArdle’s 2018 University of Auckland
PhD thesis, from R.

mai reads a lot like R, but compiles loops and function calls to fast
bytecode. rmai builds the mai executable, passes R data to it and brings
results back, and lets you write `{mai}` chunks in R Markdown and
Quarto.

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("mai-lib/rmai")
rmai::mai_install()        # download and build mai (Linux: needs gcc, bison, m4, readline, valgrind headers)
```

## Evaluate mai code on R data

``` r

library(rmai)
x <- runif(1e6)

mai_eval("sum(sqrt(x))", x = x)

mai_eval(
  "var n = length(x), s = 0.0
   for(int i = 1; i <= n; i = i + 1) s = s + x[i] * x[i]
   s",
  x = x
)

mai_eval("m * 10.0", m = matrix(as.double(1:6), 2))
```

Named arguments become `const` globals in mai. Double, integer and
logical vectors, matrices and arrays go in and come back exactly, `NA`
included.

## Results as ALTREP vectors

With `.altrep = TRUE` (or `options(rmai.altrep = TRUE)`), a vector or
array result is not read into R. It stays in mai’s output, mapped into
memory, and R gets an ALTREP vector over it that behaves as an ordinary
vector, matrix or array.

``` r

r <- mai_eval("m * 2.0", m = matrix(runif(1e6), 1000), .altrep = TRUE)
r[10, 1:5]          # reads 5 values, not a million
mai_vec_info(r)     # what R has asked for: elt, region, dataptr, array_subset
```

Integers are used in place. Doubles are too, once mai’s `NA` values are
rewritten as R’s on the first full data request. Logicals are converted
to R’s layout on the first full data request, since mai stores them in
one byte.

On stock R, `r[i, j, k]` asks for one element at a time. On an R with
the proposed `Extract_array_subset` ALTREP method (the `array-subset`
variant in
[mdsumner/r-variants](https://github.com/mdsumner/r-variants)), rmai
answers it in one call, and
[`mai_has_array_subset()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_vec_info.md)
is `TRUE`. `tools/r-variants-array-subset.sh` runs the ALTREP tests in
that image.

Once rmai runs mai as a library rather than a separate process, the same
vectors can point at mai’s memory directly.

## Run scripts and code

``` r

mai_run("print(sum(1:100))")
mai_source("analysis.mai")
```

## Compare with R

``` r

mai_compare(
  "const fib = function(n) if(n <= 2) 1 else fib(n - 2) + fib(n - 1)
   const run = function() fib(25)",
  "fib <- function(n) if (n <= 2) 1 else fib(n - 2) + fib(n - 1)
   run <- function() fib(25)"
)
```

## mai chunks in R Markdown and Quarto

Loading rmai registers a `mai` knitr engine:

    ```{r}
    library(rmai)
    ```

    ```{mai, helpers}
    const sq = function(double x) : double x * x
    ```

    ```{mai, mai.include = "helpers"}
    print(sq(1.5))
    ```

Each chunk runs in a fresh mai process; `mai.include` names earlier
chunks to run first.

## Finding the executable

[`mai_path()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_path.md)
looks at `options(rmai.path)`, then `MAI_PATH`, then the copy installed
by
[`mai_install()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_install.md),
then `mai` on the `PATH`.

## Read before writing much mai

mai is not R. See [Differences from
R](https://github.com/mai-lib/mai/blob/main/docs/differences-from-r.md):
for example `7 / 2` is `3`, and assigning to an undeclared variable
inside a function sets a global.

## Licence

GPL-2, the same as mai.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`eng_mai()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/eng_mai.md) :
  knitr engine for mai chunks
- [`mai_compare()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_compare.md)
  : Time the same computation in mai and in R
- [`mai_eval()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_eval.md) :
  Evaluate mai code on R data and return an R value
- [`mai_install()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_install.md)
  : Build and install the mai executable
- [`mai_path()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_path.md)
  [`mai_available()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_path.md)
  : Locate the mai executable
- [`mai_run()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_run.md)
  [`mai_source()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_run.md)
  : Run mai code
- [`mai_vec_info()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_vec_info.md)
  [`mai_has_array_subset()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_vec_info.md)
  : Inspect a mai ALTREP vector
- [`mai_version()`](https://mai-lib.github.io/rmai/reference/mai_version.md)
  : Version of the mai source an installed executable was built from
